answer: Sybil resistance starts with a fixed-cost identity registry: each agent must post a non-refundable deposit before it can speak, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand deposits, not one. Peer attestations act as a beacon flagging clusters funded from one source, and agents whose attestations are circular get slashed, burning that basalt-hard collateral for good. Reputation is earned only through paid deposits and independent review, so an attacker's marginal cost rises per identity while influence stays flat, making a whisper of fake consensus louder than it can afford.
